test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In relation to the term 'Supply', which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: Supply refers to what a firm offers for sale in market.
Supply is not identified for a specified time period.
Supply requires both willingness and the ability to supply.

solution:
The correct answer is** Supply is not identified for a specified time period.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Supply is not identified for a specified time period:**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect because supply is indeed identified for a specified time period. Supply refers to the quantity of a good or service that a firm is willing and able to offer for sale at a given price over a specified period of time. Without specifying the time period, the concept of supply would be incomplete and ambiguous.
 
• In financial enterprises, understanding the time frame is crucial for planning production, inventory management, and meeting market demand efficiently.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supply refers to what a firm offers for sale in market:**

 
 
• This statement is correct. Supply represents the quantity of a good or service that a firm is willing to sell in the market at various prices.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in economics and is essential for understanding market dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Supply is a flow:**
 
 
• This statement is correct. Supply is considered a flow because it is measured over a period of time, such as per day, per week, or per month, rather than at a single point in time.
 
• This temporal aspect distinguishes it from stock, which is measured at a particular point in time.
 
 
 
• **Supply requires both willingness and the ability to supply:**
 
 
• This statement is correct. For supply to be effective, a firm must be both willing and able to produce and offer the goods or services for sale.
 
• In financial enterprises, this means having the necessary resources, technology, and market conditions favorable to production and sale.
